label: Possible founded coming-to-be from founded populated pasts and possible earlier grounds (inference)
rule: In the earlier-grounded history, a never-generated contingent thing would be present at a moment with nothing earlier, where no ground can have been present before it
meaning: Non-transcription conditional support option for premise A3 prime of the modal spine, pricing horn H1 of the initial-state view. Take the accessible history in which every contingent concrete thing has an existing concrete ground and every ground of a contingent concrete thing was present before each moment of its presence. Suppose a contingent concrete thing x present at t was never absent earlier. The populated moment t has a founded past, so some moment m at or below t has no earlier moment (ContingentComingToBe.minimalBelow); x is present at m; its ground must be present strictly before m, which is impossible. So every contingent concrete thing of that history comes to be, and founded coming-to-be is possible. Both premises are OPEN, and together they already entail that possibly a necessary concrete individual exists (possiblyNecessaryOfEarlierGrounds), so this option does not help against a rival who denies that a necessary being is possible. Controls 4, 5 and 7 show the temporal priority of grounds is needed: a ground with no earlier presence (simultaneous in 4 and 5, only later in 7) lets a contingent thing be grounded and never generated; without any necessary concrete individual only with non-well-founded grounding (5, 7), the horn BruteFoundationBoundary.bruteRootOrNonWellFounded already forces. Control 3 shows founded populated pasts are needed. No premise is established.
